# Best power banks for a MacBook Pro

For a MacBook Pro, look for 100W or more of USB-C output and a capacity under 100Wh so it's allowed on flights. A 16-inch Pro only fast-charges at 140W (PD 3.1), while a 14-inch Pro is fine at about 100W ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/819438/best-macbook-usb-c-charger.html)).

## My picks

**Best overall: Anker Prime Power Bank (26,250mAh, 300W)**
- It has two 140W USB-C ports and a 300W total output, so it can fast-charge two laptops at once.
- It recharges quickly, reaching 80% in about 20 minutes with both USB-C ports plugged in.
- At 99.75Wh it's airline-legal, and it comes with a 240W USB-C cable.
- It was about $230 at launch, with deals near $200. It has no built-in cable.
- Macworld ranks it #1, and its tested 14-inch Pro charged fully with roughly 25% left for a second charge.
- [Macworld review and deal links](https://www.macworld.com/article/2395511/best-laptop-power-banks-for-apple-macbook.html) · [WIRED roundup](https://www.wired.com/story/best-laptop-power-banks/)

**Best with a built-in cable: EcoFlow RAPID Pro 27K (300W)**
- It has a retractable 140W USB-C cable, two 140W ports and two 65W ports, at 99.54Wh.
- Macworld measured 117% total charge on a 14-inch Pro (about 1.2 charges), and says to expect roughly 70–75% on a 16-inch Pro.
- It was $219.99 when reviewed, and WIRED listed it around $190 on Amazon.
- Skip the "X" version, since Macworld found it confusing and it lacks the built-in cable.
- [Macworld review](https://www.macworld.com/article/2955100/ecoflow-rapid-pro-27k-power-bank-300w-review-macbook-battery-pack.html) · [WIRED roundup](https://www.wired.com/story/best-laptop-power-banks/)

**Best value at 140W: INIU Cougar P64 (140W)**
- Macworld calls it the best value 140W pick, with a large capacity and PD 3.1. The downsides are no built-in cable and a lower total output.
- I don't have a current price for it, so check the deal links in [Macworld's roundup](https://www.macworld.com/article/2395511/best-laptop-power-banks-for-apple-macbook.html).

**Cheaper alternative: ReelCharge ReelPro (27,000mAh, 200W)**
- It has a built-in cable rated at up to 140W, and both ports are rated at 100W.
- It costs about $120 and comes with a 3-year warranty.
- ReelCharge is a new brand, which WIRED notes is a bit riskier, and recharging is slower because input maxes out at 100W.
- [WIRED roundup](https://www.wired.com/story/best-laptop-power-banks/)

**Budget pick for a 14-inch Pro: Baseus Blade H1 (20,000mAh, 100W)**
- It's flat and airline-legal at about 74Wh, and a 100W cable is included.
- It's $89.99 at Baseus, and Baseus claims 50% charge in 30 minutes.
- Per-port output when charging several devices isn't published.
- [Buy at Baseus](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah). This is an affiliate link, so the retailer pays a commission at no cost to you. [Product details](https://dealectric.com/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah)

## Quick advice
- **16-inch Pro:** Get a 140W model (Anker Prime or EcoFlow). On older 16-inch models, 140W needs Apple's USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable, because the USB-C port tops out at 100W. M4 and M5 models can also use a Thunderbolt 5 cable ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/819438/best-macbook-usb-c-charger.html)).
- **14-inch Pro:** 100W is enough, so the Baseus or ReelCharge will do.
- **Flying:** Stay under 100Wh. Even a 99Wh bank recharges a 16-inch Pro only to about 70–75% because of conversion losses.

Prices change often, so check the current price at checkout. If you tell me your MacBook model and budget, I can narrow it to one.
